title: Running fzf from $HOME causes ALL CPU cores to operate at 100% continuously when nothing is typed.
body: ### Checklist - [x] I have read through the manual page (`man fzf`) - [x] I have searched through the existing issues - [x] For bug reports, I have checked if the bug is reproducible in the latest version of fzf ### Output of `fzf --version` 0.70.0 (eacef5ea) ### OS - [x] Linux - [ ] macOS - [ ] Windows - [ ] Etc. ### Shell - [x] bash - [ ] zsh - [ ] fish ### Problem / Steps to reproduce This is what happen after the `fzf ` command is issued from $HOME and me not typing anything into the fzf interface: ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/85ef005e-1b55-4820-bf79-8aec533dcf9d) This issue of maxing out the CPU cores at 100% utilization seems to only occur when `fzf` command is issued from `$HOME` and not other directory. **2nd Attempt: 1 minute observation.** **3rd Attempt: 5 minutes observation.** 32GB RAM is nearly max out by fzf. ~20GB ram filled up in 5 minutes. Seems to be quite dangerous to run `fzf` command when in $HOME. Is this normal?

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
fzf does use multiple threads when traversing the file system using the [fastwalk](https://github.com/charlievieth/fastwalk) library.

- https://github.com/charlievieth/fastwalk/blob/99cabbde61f9f204ff24e8bc1e775a288d52a546/fastwalk.go#L67-L91

20GB for 16M entries does seem unusually high though. That is not within the expected range. On my computer, fzf takes less than 2GB for 7M entries under my home directory.

Could you try something like this to check the number of entries and the total size in bytes?

```sh
(cd ~; fd -H -L) | wc
  # 7943053 8800320 1072569518
```
(https://github.com/sharkdp/fd)

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
I confirm that FZF will run continuously with all cores at 100% utilization and not stop when walker is run with `--follow` option from $HOME directory. Its like it is in an infinite loop condition.

Using command `(cd ~; fdfind -H -L) | wc`, i.e. replacing charlievieth/fastwalk with `fd`,  will also result in all cores running at 100% utilization continuously. The difference is the RAM usage remains low and does not get max out.  

However,  when I use export `FZF_DEFAULT_COMMAND='fdfind -H -L -E ".git"'`, all cores will also run at 100% utilization continuously and RAM can also be used to near max very quickly.

Other than switching off `follow symlink`, is there another way to resolve this issue?

This infinite loop at 100% max running fzf from $HOME is expensive. On my CPU, it easily consumes an additional amount of ~70W (I see this from the power meter). Also means increase wear on SSD, which is quite costly now a days.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
> Other than switching off `follow symlink`, is there another way to resolve this issue?

Try to locate the directory causing the slowdown ideally it’s just one folder and exclude it when using `fd` (see `man fd`) or `fzf`’s built-in walker.

https://github.com/participant1/fzf/blob/b59f27ef5aba64e20d4415538fa2f460977a0cba/man/man1/fzf.1#L1273-L1275

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
> The difference is the RAM usage remains low and does not get max out.

fzf has to retain the entire input in memory for interactive filtering unlike the command which can throw away each item immediately after printing it.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
To locate the problematic symlink causing the infinite loop,  I ran this command: 
```
find -L "$HOME" -type l -print
```
The problematic link appears something like below and kept repeating.

```
find: File system loop detected; '/home/<user>/dir/sym' is part of the same file system loop as '/home/<user>' 
```
In my case, it was caused by Steam. I tried uninstalling it but the problem still persisted.  I then removed it via
```
rm -rf ~/.var/app/com.valvesoftware.Steam
```
and now when I run fzf, the infinite loop no longer occurred. 

Writing the above here to help others who may similarly experience this issue. 

I like to suggest a cautionary note of this issue be informed to user in fzf documentation. 

Thank you everyone.

If this is actually a hard problem to solve, we can think of a few workarounds:

- Limit the maximum depth of a traversal
- Add `z:` (or a better one if there's any) to the default ignore list
- Make fzf stop consuming the stream if its memory usage grows beyond a certain threshold (e.g. 70% of system memory)

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Hmm, on second thought, the fundamental problem here is that there are symlinks to an ancestor of the walker root. 

For example, if it's a link to the root directory, we'll have to go through numerous entries before we detect a cycle.

```
/home/<user>/.local/share/Steam/steamapps/compatdata/0/pfx/dosdevices/z: -> /
```
